And the plain-English version of what this whole thing is:

**What it is:** a system that learns the fingerprint of *how* you write — not what you say, but the shape of it. Sentence length, punctuation habits, how often you hedge, how fast you fire off messages, word variety. It built that fingerprint from 94,503 of your sent messages going back to 2011.

**Why it exists:** you wanted to know whether your writing measurably changes when your state changes — high, tired, wired, whatever. If the fingerprint drifts far enough from your baseline, the system raises a flag. It's an instrument, not a diagnosis.

**What it can do:** catch that your last 3 hours of writing looks statistically unlike your own history, and tell you *which* habits shifted (shorter sentences, more repetition, different rhythm). Over time, with your labels, it can learn what *your* high or *your* exhaustion looks like in text.

**What it can't do:** it can't prove you're high. A flag means "this doesn't look like your usual writing" — it could be excitement, a new topic, typing one-handed. Your labels are the only ground truth, and right now there aren't enough of them to name any state's signature. That's exactly what the hotkey is for.

Plenty. The landmark pass is the expensive part and you already pay for it once, so most of this is free:

- **Blendshapes** — FaceLandmarker spits out 52 of them alongside the landmarks. Smile intensity, brow raise, jaw open, cheek puff — a whole expression/emotion channel you're currently throwing away.
- **Symmetry map** — mirror the mesh, score bilateral deviation per region. You excluded asymmetry as selfie-roll noise in the warp work; a proper roll-corrected symmetry score is its own instrument.
- **Neoclassical canons** — facial thirds, fifths, golden-ratio checks on nose/mouth/eye spacing. Cheap ratios, fun to display.
- **Skin telemetry** — wrinkle density, under-eye darkness, skin evenness and redness/yellowness from cheek pixel stats in Lab space. Lighting-dependent, but there's real literature behind the health-attraction link.
- **Face-shape classifier** — oval/round/square/heart/oblong from the width ratios. Trivial once you have the mesh.
- **Head pose as quality gate** — roll/pitch/yaw weighting every measurement's confidence. Your selfie-roll problem, solved structurally.
- **Catalog match** — the killer one for you specifically: compare the new vector against your 155-face attraction catalog and surface the closest faces plus how you rated them. Preference prediction grounded in your own data instead of generic beauty scores.

Honest limits: it's one frontal 2D photo, so anything needing true depth (tip projection, gonial angle) is a proxy at best, and skin stuff needs decent lighting or it's noise.
